note: the echoed request id stops being compared with the one that was minted, so a superseded or replayed reply is accepted on both hops. 04-VALIDATION names this clause as requestApply's ONLY staleness key — the apply reply is deliberately not generation-guarded — so its deletion is the whole staleness failure on that path (04-REVIEW WR-02, T-04G-27)

requestStatus's combined shape-and-diagnosis gate never holds, so no status reply is ever refused and any object reaching the worker becomes a diagnosis about the agent's view. Fences the gate as a whole; the individual clauses inside validDiagnosis are fenced by request-id-echo and diagnosis-pairing (04-REVIEW WR-02, T-04G-28)

an unpaired {diagnosis, reason} becomes renderable. ICONS is keyed by status alone while TITLES is keyed by the whole pair, so the artwork write SUCCEEDS and the title write carries no value — one state's artwork under no sentence at all, which is the FAIL-05 failure mode. MEASURED killed on the clean-fallback behavioural test's toolbar equality, which carries both halves at once (icons/missing.png under an undefined title). The separate no-valueless-title invariant in the same test guards that second half but is NOT the assertion that fires here, because the toolbar equality precedes it (04-REVIEW WR-05, T-04G-29)

requestEnabled stops checking that the worker's reply carries an in-set status and a boolean-or-null preference, so a buggy worker's unrecognised value is rendered instead of reported as a failed save. Fences the popup's own second line of defence on the set-enabled path only; refresh's gate has the same two clauses in the opposite order and is a distinct literal (04-REVIEW WR-02, T-04G-30)

render indexes the copy map directly, so an unpaired-but-individually-valid pair writes no sentence into the status region instead of reporting the connection fact. This is the popup-side mirror of diagnosis-pairing and is what keeps a malformed state from being blamed on the agent's view (04-REVIEW WR-05, T-04G-30)
